title: State Space Models for Realtime Multimodal Intelligence: Karan Goel

summary: Karan Goel, founder/CEO of Cartesia, argues that AI has been dominated by batch intelligence for the past four to five years—systems that reason for extended periods before solving problems. He advocates a shift toward real-time, streaming intelligence where models respond instantly to continuous inputs like audio, video, and sensor streams. Key applications include conversational voice interfaces, on-device assistants running at low power, real-time world generation analogous to GPU-rendered graphics, and robotics that ingest and respond to multimodal sensor data instantly. Goel's central thesis is that multimodal AI requires efficient long-context modeling. Text is already fairly compressed, but audio, video, and sensor data produce massive token sequences. Current Transformer models scale quadratically with context length, are optimized for data centers, and rely on keeping all context and retrieving from it rather than compressing information as humans do. Goel estimates humans process approximately 1 billion text tokens, 10 billion audio tokens, and 1 trillion video tokens per year on a low-power biological computer, while today's best models handle only 10 million to 100 million tokens. Cartesia's approach uses State Space Models (SSMs), including Mamba as a recent iteration, which scale linearly in context length, compress information as it arrives, and enable low-power, low-memory implementations. SSMs function as streaming systems: tokens flow in, update an internal memory state, and are then discarded, creating a compressed representation analogous to a zip file inside the model. This recurrence-based approach mirrors human reasoning and contrasts with Transformer retrieval. Goel notes SSMs are gaining adoption and will play a larger role as multimodal data becomes more important over the next three to five years. On quality, he acknowledges a trade-off between compression and retaining all information, but argues compression helps for large-context and multimodal problems—compressing 24 hours of security footage on the fly helps solve tasks better than re-examining all footage each time. SSM quality is strong for long-context and multimodal problems, though less advantageous for short context. Cartesia recently released a text-to-speech voice generation model with dramatically reduced latency, delivering instant voice responses from the data center. They are also working to run these models on Mac and other devices at low power, matching the data-center experience on any device. A demo is available at play.ai.

sections.title: Batch vs. Real-Time Intelligence Paradigm
sections.summary: Goel frames the last 4-5 years of AI as focused on batch intelligence—systems that reason for long periods before solving problems. He contrasts this with streaming/real-time intelligence for audio, video, and sensor streams, noting a shift from batch APIs toward low-latency real-time querying.

sections.title: Real-Time Applications and Use Cases
sections.summary: Applications of real-time intelligence include conversational voice interfaces, on-device assistants running at low power on phones or laptops, real-time world generation for gaming analogous to GPU rendering, and robotics that ingest audio/video/sensor data and respond instantly. Use cases span customer support agents, health insurance Q&A, shipment coordination, and other automatable coordination tasks.

sections.title: Cartesia's Approach and SSM Origins
sections.summary: Goel introduces Cartesia's work on real-time foundation models built on State Space Models. He traces the technology to his Stanford PhD work under advisor Chris, developing early SSM precursors, with Mamba as a more recent widely-known iteration. The approach seeks new architectures beyond the standard Transformer recipe.

sections.title: Long Context, Compression vs. Retrieval
sections.summary: Efficiently modeling long context is a core problem. Text is already fairly compressed, but audio, video, and sensor data (e.g., a day of security camera footage) produce massive sequences. Current AI systems rely on retrieval—keeping all context—rather than compression, which Goel sees as fundamental to intelligence. Humans can remember events from 30 years ago without retrieval mechanisms.

sections.title: Human Processing Capacity and AI Gaps
sections.summary: Goel estimates humans process ~1 billion text tokens, ~10 billion audio tokens, and ~1 trillion video tokens per year simultaneously on a low-power biological computer. Today's best AI models handle only 10M-100M tokens. He argues intelligence is far from solved and the goal is building long-lived machines that compress and understand information over very long periods.

sections.title: Transformer Limitations and SSM Advantages
sections.summary: Transformers are built for data centers with quadratic scaling in context length, making multimodal inference (which has far more tokens than text) prohibitively expensive at scale. Cartesia's SSMs have compression at their core, scale linearly in context length, use low memory, and enable massive context and low-power implementations. The working intuition: Transformers attend to every past token quadratically, while SSMs compress information as it arrives.

sections.title: SSM Streaming Architecture and Adoption Outlook
sections.summary: Goel explains SSMs as streaming systems: tokens flow in, update an internal memory state, and are discarded, simplifying the system by avoiding storage of all past context. This recurrence-based compression, analogous to a zip file inside the model, mirrors human reasoning. SSMs are gaining adoption, and Goel predicts they will play a larger role in the next three to five years as multimodal data and efficiency demands grow.

sections.title: SSM Quality Trade-offs and Cartesia Product Release
sections.summary: Goel addresses quality, noting a trade-off between compression and retaining all information, but argues compression helps for large-context and multimodal problems—compressing 24 hours of security footage on the fly aids task performance better than re-examining all footage. SSM quality excels for long-context and multimodal tasks but is less advantageous for short context. Cartesia recently released a low-latency text-to-speech voice generation model with instant data-center response, and is working to run these models on Mac and other devices at low power. A demo is available at play.ai.
